newAssets.title: Seltice, Chief of the Coeur D’Alênes, 1891
newAssets.credit: Olin Levi Warner, 1891. Smithsonian American Art Museum, A Gift of Alison Warner Waterman in memory of her mother, Frances D. Warner, 1985.76.3. Public domain.
newAssets.creator: Olin Levi Warner; museum photographer not individually named in the inspected record
newAssets.rightsLabel: Public domain — SAAM item marked Free to use
newAssets.scope: Museum photograph of Olin Levi Warner’s 1891 bronze portrait relief of the specifically identified Coeur d’Alene leader Seltice. This is an outside sculptor’s historical portrait, not Coeur d’Alene-made art, a photograph of the living sitter, or a present government representation. The museum’s curators place Warner’s portraits in the context of racial classification and an erroneous expectation that Native peoples would disappear, and note that the sitters’ perspectives are poorly documented. That context is retained; no essential cultural or physical trait is inferred from the portrait. No traditional design meanings or community endorsement are claimed.
newAssets.alt: A round bronze relief with a right-facing portrait of Seltice and lettering identifying him as a Coeur d’Alene chief.

newAssets.title: Kootenai National Wildlife Refuge wetlands, Idaho, 2022
newAssets.credit: Carlene Hardt, June 29, 2022. U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service media collection; item designated Public Domain.
newAssets.creator: Carlene Hardt
newAssets.rightsLabel: Public Domain — explicit FWS item designation; no CC0 license asserted
newAssets.scope: Modern public-refuge wetland scene in the Kootenai River valley near Bonners Ferry, Idaho. The Kootenai Tribe of Idaho’s history places its continuing community and allotments along the Kootenai River and surrounding uplands. The FWS refuge account locates the photographed facility near Bonners Ferry, adjacent to the river’s west banks. This supports narrow Idaho regional/environmental context in the broader cross-border Kootenai/Ktunaxa collection; the photograph is not a picture of tribal members, reservation land, an identified cultural site, all Ktunaxa communities or a homeland boundary. The relationship comes from those inspected accounts, not merely the refuge sharing the name Kootenai. No legal rights or jurisdiction determination is made.
newAssets.alt: Green wetland vegetation surrounds open water in Kootenai National Wildlife Refuge, with a wooded valley and mountains beneath a cloudy blue sky.
